claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me: **How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So I'm assessing eligibility for your son **Alex**, who is 8 years old.

Before I can determine your eligibility, I need to gather some information about your circumstances. Let me start with the first question:

**Are you Alex's parent or guardian, and do you live with him in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm his parent, yes, and I live in the UK. But Alex doesn't actually live with me - he lives with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. So Alex lives with his mum rather than with you.

To help me understand your situation better:

**Does Alex's mum claim Child Benefit for him, or do you know if anyone else is claiming it?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, his mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I appreciate you providing that information. Before I make my final assessment, let me check the detailed eligibility rules to ensure I give you accurate guidance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for waiting. Based on the eligibility rules I've reviewed, I now have a clear picture of your situation.

Since Alex lives with his mum and she is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you would **not be eligible** to also claim Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

According to the rules, only one person can get Child Benefit for a child. Since Alex's mum is already the person claiming Child Benefit for him, you cannot also claim for the same child.

However, you could potentially continue receiving Child Benefit if you were making financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep (such as food, clothes, pocket money, or financial contributions to his accommodation) **and** you stopped claiming so that his mum could claim instead. But that would still mean Alex's mum would be the one receiving the benefit payments, not you.

Is there anything else you'd like to clarify about this, or are there any other children you'd like me to assess eligibility for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, that's all I needed to know. Thank you for explaining it to me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help clarify the situation for you. Let me document the outcome of our assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: If you have any further questions in the future, feel free to reach out. All the best!
